parsed.explanation: Combined regime is mixed. Strong state/provincial protections—public-accommodation enforcement, open identity documents, police gender-X reporting, bias-crime tools, healthcare shield for travellers, safest-per-capita violence record—lower everyday local exposure. But federal passport/visa binary rules, visa evidence demands, fraud/permanent-ineligibility findings, government-facility exclusions, hostile minors/care policies, and severe immigration/corrections custody harms remain operative. A document mismatch can escalate into denial, investigation, detention, or deportation. State law is not documented to pre-empt border, federal facilities, or federal custody. For an outed adult, entry and emergency custody carry high consequences; a trans minor/guardian faces added federal child-policy exposure despite local care protection.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal order bars self-selected passport/visa sex, ends new X markers, adds visa case notes, permits refusal and evidence demands, and can treat suspected misrepresentation as fraud/permanent ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; state permits M/F/X licences and birth certificates without medical proof; legal-aid FAQ and litigation exist.
entry_documents.interaction: State identity documents do not bind federal border screening; discrepancy can lead to visa denial, investigation, removal, and custody exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal custody practices include conversion-therapy-like removal of hormones and hair control; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse; other facilities criminalise bathroom use.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime law exists; state bias enhancements and police gender-X reporting may help outside detention; no documented state custody remedy.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border document mismatch can escalate into immigration detention where severe federal custody harms dominate despite local protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; many jurisdictions restrict school/public facilities and some criminalise use.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province bans service and facility denial in public accommodations, is most-protective tier, has gender-X police data; no local bathroom ban documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State public-accommodation law may protect hotels/restaurants but does not show operative pre-emption of federal government-facility rules.

care_services.exposure: Federal policies restrict minors’ gender-affirming care, shut youth services, subpoena under-19 medical records, threaten funding and prosecutions; custody may interrupt medication.
care_services.protection: State executive order directs agencies to protect gender-affirming healthcare for people travelling in; hospital records protect orientation/gender identity; documents are inclusive.
care_services.interaction: Care access is shielded within state for visitors, but federal health-record subpoenas, minors policies, and detention can override or complicate care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism language prioritises neutralising groups called radically pro-transgender; gender ideology is framed as extremist; public polls support birth-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State abolished panic defence, bias sentencing, police gender-X reporting, protective-tier laws, and official apology for historic harassment.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat framing legitimises border scrutiny and detention; state enforcement can counter local hostility but not federal actions.

minors_guardians.exposure: National hostility targets minors’ care, youth services, school staff, and records; local parental-notification policies may out students; entry documents affect minors.
minors_guardians.protection: State protects healthcare for travellers, requires privacy in hospital records, supports names/pronouns/facilities in school guidance, and recognises marriages.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardians gain local care protection, but federal border documents, school notification, and record-subpoena uncertainty persist for trans minors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National trans-women killings are numerous; no visitor-specific local assault data, so frequency of street violence against travellers is not documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State dataset places it among safest per-capita; bias enhancements, police gender-X data, national hate-crime statute, and public-accommodation protections exist.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local violence appears comparatively low, but absence of complaint/prosecution data leaves police response quality uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unresolved litigation over passport and executive orders, missing complaint statistics, uncertain custody placement, facility-map caveats, and school-notification outcome unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-rights agency, legal-aid guidance, state protective law, hate-crime statute, litigation challenges, and foreign advisories may support planning.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: State remedies may help service denial, but no documented operative remedy covers federal border screening, custody, or health-record subpoenas.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar to 0.45-D because a universal federal screening/document exposure remains without clear remedy. Lower on everyday local service risk due protective state law, but higher on visa fraud/immigration-custody consequences.

Below 0.55-D because the entry regime is active and hostile, not merely uneven private service refusals. Local care shield and safer violence data pull it partly back up, but border/federal custody exposure dominates.

Well below 0.75-C because that anchor has a dead-letter sexuality law and functioning remedies with no active federal document/custody restriction; this dossier has operative federal restrictions and severe detention harms.

parsed.synthesis: Federal document and custody hostility dominates the worst-case journey: visa and passport rules make trans status an adjudication issue, and escalation can produce severe unmitigated immigration or corrections harms. State protections meaningfully lower in-state everyday exposure for lodging, care access, identity documents, police reporting, and street violence. These are not documented to pre-empt border screening, federal facilities, or federal detention. The operative regime is therefore conditional: relatively protective inside the division, high risk at entry or custody. Missing enforcement data keeps the rating elevated-risk rather than reduced-risk.
